newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon cuts GM estimates.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon cuts GM estimates.

text.p: -- Salomon Brothers auto analyst Jack Kirnan said he reduced his fourth-quarter and full-year earnings estimate by $650 million, or $0.85 a share, because of lost production caused by strikes in the United States and Canada.

-- In a research report, Kirnan said his fourth quarter earnings per share estimate is now $1.00 a share, while his 1996 full-year estimate is $5.80. His 1997 GM earnings per share forecast is unchanged at $7.50.

-- Earlier on Monday, GM announced that it reduced its fourth-quarter North American production forecast by 151,000 units because of production lost to the U.S. and Canadian walkouts in October, including 113,000 cars and 38,000 trucks.

-- Kirnan said GM would be hard-pressed to make up any lost production in the fourth quarter. But despite the strikes, he estimated that GM would end the fourth quarter with $14 billion in cash on its balance sheet, down only marginally from $14.50 billion at the end of the third quarter.

-- Kirnan added he believed there was a better than 50 percent chance that GM's board of directors would authorise a share repurchase programme that could approach $2 billion or more. He continues to rate GM shares a "buy" and looks for them to reach 65 in the next 12 months.
GM shares closed off 1/2 at 55 on the New York Stock Exchange Monday.
